questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

A. Having been a part of the team for five years, B. the promotion to manager was C. unexpected but much appreciated D. by him.

options.text: Having been a part of the team for five years,

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. the promotion to manager was .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The grammatical error lies in part 2, **"the promotion to manager was".**
 
• The sentence starts with **"Having been a part of the team for five years,"**, which sets the context for the subject of the sentence. However, part 2 incorrectly makes **"the promotion"** the subject.
 
• Instead, the subject should be **"he"** or the person being referred to, as the promotion is related to him.

Correct sentence: *Having been a part of the team for five years, he found the promotion to manager unexpected but much appreciated.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** Ensure the subject of the sentence aligns correctly with the verb.
 
• **Misplaced Modifiers:** Avoid making the wrong part of the sentence the subject when a modifier sets a different context.
 
• **Clarity:** Revising for clarity ensures the sentence conveys the intended meaning accurately.
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

He said that while he had been writing the report, his laptop suddenly shut down.

options.text: He said, "While I wrote the report, my laptop suddenly shut down."
He said, "While I was writing the report, my laptop suddenly shut down."
He said, "While I am writing the report, my laptop suddenly shuts down."
He said, "While I had been writing the report, my laptop had shut down."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. He said, "While I was writing the report, my laptop suddenly shut down."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **Reported Speech**, which needs to be converted into **Direct Speech**.
 
• In the Direct Speech format, the tense used depends on the context and the tense of the original statement.
 
• From the sentence in Reported Speech:
 
 
• Original tense: "had been writing" (past perfect continuous) → converted to "was writing" (past continuous) for Direct Speech.
 
• The event "laptop suddenly shut down" is in simple past tense ("shut down").
 
 
 
• Option 2 correctly reflects the tense consistency and retains the original meaning of the sentence.

Correct sentence: *He said, "While I was writing the report, my laptop suddenly shut down."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Direct Speech:**
 
 
• Direct Speech is used to quote the exact words of the speaker.
 
• It is enclosed in quotation marks (" ").
 
• Example: He said, "I am going to the market."
 
 
 
• **Reported Speech:**
 
 
• Reported Speech is used to convey the meaning of what the speaker said, without quoting their exact words.
 
• It typically involves a shift in tense and no quotation marks.
 
• Example: He said that he was going to the market.

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

Is the new policy expected to be implemented immediately across all departments?

options.text: Are they expecting to implement the new policy immediately across all departments?
Is the new policy implementing immediately across all departments?
Do they expect to implement the new policy immediately across all departments?
They expect to implement the new policy immediately across all departments?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Do they expect to implement the new policy immediately across all departments? .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **passive voice**. To change it to the **active voice**, we need to identify the implied subject, which in this case is “they.”
 
• The sentence structure in active voice should follow the pattern: **Subject + Verb + Object**.
 
• The correct option, Option 3, rephrases the sentence in the active form as: **Do they expect to implement the new policy immediately across all departments?**
 
• The other options are incorrect because:
 
 
• **Option 1: Are they expecting to implement the new policy immediately across all departments?** - Incorrect because it uses the present continuous, which is not needed here.
 
• **Option 2: Is the new policy implementing immediately across all departments?** - Incorrect because it remains in the passive form and is grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 4: They expect to implement the new policy immediately across all departments?** - Incorrect because it is not in the interrogative form as required by the original question.
 
 

Correct sentence: *Do they expect to implement the new policy immediately across all departments?*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active vs Passive Voice:**
 
 
• **Active voice:** The subject performs the action (e.g., “They expect to implement the policy.”).
 
• **Passive voice:** The subject receives the action (e.g., “The policy is expected to be implemented.”).
 
 
 
• While changing from passive to active voice, always identify the doer of the action and restructure the sentence accordingly.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.**

My mother said, "I will help you with your homework."

options.text: My mother said that she would help me with my homework.
My mother said that she will help me with my homework.
My mother said that she would have helped me with my homework.
My mother said that she helped me with my homework.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. My mother said that she would help me with my homework .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in direct speech and needs to be converted into indirect speech.
 
• In indirect speech, the tense of the verb changes to reflect the fact that the statement is being reported.
 
• Here, the direct speech statement **“I will help you with your homework”** is in the future tense.
 
• When converting to indirect speech, the future tense **‘will’** changes to **‘would’**.
 
• Thus, the correct indirect speech sentence is **“My mother said that she would help me with my homework.”**

Correct sentence: *My mother said that she would help me with my homework.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for Changing Direct to Indirect Speech:**
 
 
• **Pronouns:** Pronouns are adjusted based on the subject and object of the reporting sentence.
 
• **Verb Tense:** The verb tense is shifted back one step in time (e.g., present to past, future to conditional).
 
• **Time and Place Words:** Words indicating time and place are changed to match the perspective of the speaker (e.g., “now” becomes “then,” “here” becomes “there”).
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• Direct: She said, “I am going to the market.”
 
• Indirect: She said that she was going to the market.
 
• Direct: He said, “I will finish the project tomorrow.”
 
• Indirect: He said that he would finish the project the next day.

questions.question:
Identify the voice of the verb phrase in the sentence:

"The compulsion to deliver flawless outputs within unforgiving timeframes frequently compels professionals to forsake personal well-being."

__
 
• **Active Voice Identification:** In the active voice, the subject of the sentence performs the action. Here, **"The compulsion..."** is the subject acting upon the object, **"professionals"**.
 
• **Verb Analysis:** The verb **"compels"** is in its active form. It does not use auxiliary verbs like "is/are" combined with a past participle (e.g., "are compelled"), which would indicate a passive construction.
 
• **Sentence Structure:** The sentence follows a clear **Subject + Verb + Object** pattern, emphasizing the direct impact of work pressure on individuals.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Passive Conversion:** To change this to passive voice, the object would become the subject: *"Professionals are frequently compelled by the compulsion to deliver..."*.
 
• **Contextual Meaning:** The passage highlights the **deleterious effects** of incessant work, such as **cardiac arrests and strokes**, which are often ignored due to societal stigma.
 
• **Clarion Call:** The author concludes that the rising mortality among CAs is a **clarion call** for systemic reforms and institutional accountability.

questions.question:
In the following sentence, identify the finite verb(s):

"The pandemic further **aggravated **these conditions by **transitioning **most work to virtual platforms, **blurring **the boundaries between professional and personal life, and **extending **working hours indefinitely."

In the above sentence, identify the **finite verb(s)**:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Finite Verb Definition:** A finite verb is a verb that has a specific subject and shows **tense** (past, present, or future) and **number** (singular or plural). It acts as the main verb of a clause.
 
• **Analysis of "Aggravated":** In the sentence, **"aggravated"** is the finite verb because it is the main action performed by the subject ("The pandemic") and is in the **simple past tense**.
 
• **Non-Finite Verbs:** The words **transitioning**, **blurring**, and **extending** are present participles (gerunds/participles acting as objects of the preposition "by"). They do not show tense on their own and do not have a direct subject-verb agreement in this structure, making them **non-finite**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Identifying Finite Verbs:** You can identify a finite verb by checking if it changes when you change the tense (e.g., *"The pandemic **aggravates**..."*) or the subject number.
 
• **Contextual Vocabulary:** The word **"aggravated"** in the passage means to make a problem or injury worse or more serious.
 
• **Sentence Structure:** The subject is **"The pandemic,"** the finite verb is **"aggravated,"** and the rest of the sentence provides additional information through participial phrases.

questions.question: The word "**deleterious**" in the sentence "The deleterious effects of incessant work pressures are exacerbated during the fiscal year-end and tax filing seasons, where the workload intensifies manifold" most nearly means:

__
 
• **Contextual Meaning:** In the passage, the word **"deleterious"** is used to describe the effects of incessant work pressures that lead to grave health repercussions like cardiac arrests and strokes. These consequences are inherently negative and damaging.
 
• **Definition:** **Deleterious** means causing harm or damage. It is often used in formal or technical contexts to describe something that has a destructive effect on health or systems.
 
• **Synonyms:** Common synonyms include **harmful**, detrimental, injurious, and damaging. In this context, "harmful" is the most direct and accurate substitute.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Antonym:** The opposite of deleterious is **beneficial** (Option 1) or advantageous, which clearly does not fit the context of life-threatening health conditions.
 
• **Insignificant:** Option 3 is incorrect because the passage emphasizes that these effects are "grave" and "life-threatening," making them highly significant.
 
• **Usage in Passage:** The author uses strong vocabulary like **exacerbated** (made worse) and **deleterious** to underscore the severity of the crisis facing Chartered Accountants in India.

questions.question: The phrase "**a clarion call**" in the passage most nearly means:

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. He took a very thin slice of a tissue sample and placed it on a glass slide.

Q. He added a single drop of a staining solution to make the cells visible.

R. He carefully placed a thin cover slip over the sample to protect it.

S. He placed the slide under the microscope to begin his examination.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. P, Q, R, S .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence parts need to be arranged in a sequence that forms a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
 
• **Step 1 (P):** The paragraph begins with the action of taking a thin slice of a tissue sample and placing it on a glass slide.
 
• **Step 2 (Q):** Following this, a single drop of staining solution is added to make the cells visible.
 
• **Step 3 (R):** After that, a thin cover slip is carefully placed over the sample to protect it.
 
• **Step 4 (S):** Finally, the slide is placed under the microscope to begin the examination.

Correct paragraph: *He took a very thin slice of a tissue sample and placed it on a glass slide. He added a single drop of a staining solution to make the cells visible. He carefully placed a thin cover slip over the sample to protect it. He placed the slide under the microscope to begin his examination.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When rearranging sentences, it is important to identify the logical sequence of actions or events.

questions.question:
Which word is nearest in meaning to client?

The astrologer knew that the man in front of him was no ordinary client.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. Customer .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"client"** refers to someone who purchases goods or services from a professional or a business.
 
• In the given context, the sentence mentions a man approaching an astrologer, which implies a professional-client relationship.
 
• Among the options provided:
 
 
• **Leader:** Refers to someone who guides or inspires others.
 
• **Stranger:** Refers to someone unknown or unfamiliar.
 
• **Rival:** Refers to a competitor or opponent.
 
• **Customer:** Refers to someone who buys goods or services, which is closest in meaning to "client."
 
 

Correct Explanation: *The astrologer knew that the man in front of him was no ordinary client. Here, "client" is synonymous with "customer," which fits the context of the sentence.*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding Synonyms:**
 
 
• Synonyms are words with similar meanings.
 
• Choosing the correct synonym depends on the context in which the word is used.
 
 
 
• **Examples of "Client" Usage:**
 
 
• The lawyer discussed the case with her client.
 
• The IT firm provided services to international clients.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following terms refers to the absence of government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Anarchy .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Anarchy** refers to a state of society where there is no governing authority or government.
 
• It represents complete freedom from rules or laws imposed by a governing body.
 
• This is distinct from other forms of government like **Democracy** (rule by the people), **Monarchy** (rule by a king or queen), or **Oligarchy** (rule by a small group of individuals).

Correct sentence: *The absence of government is referred to as **Anarchy**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Democracy:** A form of government where the power lies with the people who elect representatives.
 
• **Monarchy:** A system where a monarch (king or queen) rules over the state.
 
• **Oligarchy:** A government where a small group of people hold power.
</ul
